question: A shopkeeper marked an item at ₹4,000. He earns a profit of 20% after selling it with a 10% discount on the marked price. If he sells it at a price of ₹100 less than the marked price, then what is his profit percentage?
solution:
**Given:**

A shopkeeper marked an item at Rs 4,000.

He earns a profit of 20% after selling it with a 10% discount on the marked price.

He sells it at a price of Rs100 less than the marked price.

**Formula used:**

Selling Price (Sp) = Cp + ((Profit)/(100)) × Cp

Market Price (Mp) - Discount = Sp

Cp = ((100)/(100space+space profitspace Percent)) × Sp

**Calculation:**

The Sp of the article = 4000 × 90 /100

⇒ Rs 3600

He earns a profit of 20 % 

So the Cp of the article = 3600 × 100 /120

⇒ Rs 3000

If he sells it at a price of ₹100 less than the marked price, then sp will be (4000 - 100) = 3900

Profit will be 3900 - 3000 = 900

So the profit percentage will be (900 / 3000) × 100 = 30%

**∴ His profit percentage will be 30**

Profit is calculated on Cost Price.

And Discount is calculated on Market Price.
